summary.text: A 59-year-old man with a 10 pack-year smoking history presented to the emergency department with progressive, disabling NYHA III dyspnea and a lipothymic episode on minimal exertion, and was admitted to the cardiac care unit. Examination showed severe bradycardia of 30 beats per minute, elevated jugular venous pressure and basal crackles. ECGs showed junctional then sinus bradycardia with a 2s sinus pause, left anterior fascicular block and low limb-lead voltage.

Laboratory tests showed elevated potassium, impaired renal function and raised BNP and troponin. Echocardiography showed marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with a speckled septum, bi-atrial dilatation and an ejection fraction of 65%; coronary angiography excluded coronary artery disease. Cardiac MRI showed subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement compatible with cardiac amyloidosis, and Holter monitoring showed non-sustained ventricular tachycardia with sinus node dysfunction.

During hospitalization he had a hemodynamically unstable sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia terminated by 200J biphasic cardioversion, followed by temporary transvenous pacing. The next day a second polymorphic episode was treated with cardioversion and intravenous amiodarone, and an ICD was implanted for secondary prevention. The initial outcome was favorable and he was asymptomatic.

Salivary gland biopsy showed Congo red positive amyloid deposits with green birefringence, serum electrophoresis showed an IgA-Lambda monoclonal protein of 731mg/l, and bone marrow biopsy showed 67% plasma cell involvement, establishing AL cardiac amyloidosis secondary to multiple myeloma. A few days after ICD placement the device intervened in one ventricular fibrillation episode. The patient died after a few weeks, before systemic chemotherapy.
